organisms.name: Vibrio cholerae
organisms.description: Pathogenic bacterium causing cholera. Thrives in warm brackish waters with 5–30 ppt salinity.
organisms.impactNote: WHO: 1.3–4M cholera cases/year globally; shellfish bioaccumulation is primary marine vector.
organisms.source: Huq et al. (2005) Applied & Env. Micro. 71(8):4645; Colwell (1996) Science 274:2025

organisms.name: Alexandrium tamarense
organisms.description: Toxic dinoflagellate producing saxitoxin (PSP). Forms harmful algal blooms in temperate waters.
organisms.impactNote: FAO: PSP responsible for 2,000+ poisoning cases and 80+ deaths per year globally.
organisms.source: Anderson et al. (2012) Ann. Rev. Mar. Sci. 4:143–176; Hallegraeff (1993) Phycologia 32:79

organisms.name: Dreissena polymorpha
organisms.description: Prolific freshwater/low-salinity invader. Adults filter 1L water/day, disrupting food webs.
organisms.impactNote: Estimated $1B+/year damage in North America alone (Pimentel et al. 2005).
organisms.source: Hebert et al. (1989) Can. J. Fish. Aquat. Sci. 46:1587; Karatayev et al. (2007)

organisms.name: Mnemiopsis leidyi
organisms.description: Invasive comb jelly native to western Atlantic. Devastated Black Sea anchovy fishery in 1980s.
organisms.impactNote: Collapsed Black Sea anchovy catch from 204,000t to 200t (Kideys 2002).
organisms.source: Shiganova (1998) J. Mar. Biol. Assoc. UK 78:1069; Purcell et al. (2001)

organisms.name: Asterias amurensis
organisms.description: Voracious predator of bivalves, introduced to Australia via ballast water in the 1980s.
organisms.impactNote: Estimated 30 million individuals in Derwent Estuary alone (Buttermore et al. 1994).
organisms.source: Byrne et al. (1997) Mar. Biol. 127:99; Ross et al. (2003)

organisms.name: Carcinus maenas
organisms.description: One of the world's 100 worst invasive species (IUCN). Native to NE Atlantic, spread globally.
organisms.impactNote: Causes $22M/year damage to shellfish industry on US east coast (Lovell et al. 2007).
organisms.source: Carlton & Cohen (2003) J. Biogeography 30:1809; Grosholz & Ruiz (1996)

organisms.name: Undaria pinnatifida
organisms.description: Invasive kelp native to NW Pacific. Now established on 6 continents. Smothers native algae.
organisms.impactNote: Listed among 100 worst invasive species globally (Lowe et al. 2000, IUCN GISD).
organisms.source: Casas et al. (2004) Botanica Marina 47:328; Hay & Luckens (1987)

organisms.name: Pseudo-nitzschia spp.
organisms.description: Pennate diatom producing domoic acid (DA) — potent neurotoxin causing amnesic shellfish poisoning.
organisms.impactNote: 2015 US West Coast bloom: largest ever recorded. Closed fisheries across 3 states.
organisms.source: Trainer et al. (2012) Harmful Algae 14:271–300; Bates et al. (1998)

organisms.name: Gymnodinium catenatum
organisms.description: Chain-forming dinoflagellate producing PSP toxins. Can form resting cysts that survive in ballast sediment.
organisms.impactNote: Introduced to Tasmania via ballast water (Hallegraeff & Bolch 1992). Now endemic.
organisms.source: Hallegraeff & Bolch (1992) J. Plankton Res. 14:1067; Bolch & Hallegraeff (1990)

organisms.name: Enterococcus faecalis
organisms.description: Faecal indicator bacterium used globally for water quality assessment (WHO/EPA standards).
organisms.impactNote: High counts trigger beach closures and shellfish bed shutdowns worldwide.
organisms.source: WHO (2003) Guidelines for Safe Recreational Water; EPA (2012) RWQC

treatmentMethods.name: UV Irradiation
treatmentMethods.description: Medium-pressure UV lamps damage DNA/RNA, preventing organism reproduction. IMO-approved as non-active substance.
treatmentMethods.strengths: Zero chemical residuals (TRO = 0). Instant treatment. Low OPEX. No DBP formation.
treatmentMethods.limitations: Effectiveness drops when UVT < 50% (turbidity > 15 NTU). Limited vs. hard-shelled larvae. 40–80 mJ/cm² required dose.
treatmentMethods.source: IMO MEPC.300(72); Optimarin Type Approval Test Report (DNV GL 2018); EPA ETV Protocol 4.6

treatmentMethods.name: Electrochlorination
treatmentMethods.description: Electrolytic generation of NaOCl from seawater. Active substance approved under G9 Guidelines.
treatmentMethods.strengths: Broad-spectrum efficacy regardless of turbidity. Effective in all salinities > 1 ppt.
treatmentMethods.limitations: Generates TRO (0.05–0.2 mg/L) requiring neutralization before discharge. DBP formation (THMs). Reduced efficiency in cold water < 5°C.
treatmentMethods.source: IMO MEPC.300(72) G9 Guidelines; Alfa Laval PureBallast Type Approval (Lloyd's Register 2019)

treatmentMethods.name: Hybrid (UV + Electrochlorination)
treatmentMethods.description: Two-stage treatment: UV pre-disinfection + low-dose chemical polishing. Maximizes kill across all organism types.
treatmentMethods.strengths: Highest verified effectiveness (>97% for all organism classes). Minimal residual TRO (0.03–0.05 mg/L).
treatmentMethods.limitations: Higher CAPEX and system complexity. Dual maintenance requirements.
treatmentMethods.source: Werschkun et al. (2014) Water Research 57:247; Gregg et al. (2009) Mar. Poll. Bull. 58:150
